claims.text: Resistance to time-dependent plastic deformation in HEA multilayer coatings is primarily governed by internal stress fields at amorphous–nanocrystalline interfaces.
Internal stress fields at amorphous–nanocrystalline interfaces inhibit dislocation propagation.
Internal stress fields at amorphous–nanocrystalline interfaces inhibit grain-boundary sliding.
Amorphous and nanocrystalline layers have a significant contrast in elastic modulus.
Amorphous and nanocrystalline layers have a significant contrast in atomic packing density.
Mismatch between amorphous and nanocrystalline phases generates internal stress fields at their interfaces.
Interference with dislocation propagation and grain-boundary sliding retards time-dependent plastic deformation.
Alternating amorphous–nanocrystalline coatings will exhibit lower creep strain than chemically equivalent uniform-phase HEA coatings under identical loading.
Alternating amorphous–nanocrystalline coatings will exhibit greater resistance to plastic deformation than uniform-phase HEA coatings.
Phase-induced internal stress fields remain effective at room temperature and at approximately 100–200°C.
Behavior may deviate outside the stated temperature regime or under substantially altered processing conditions.
Residual stress and grain-boundary-sliding effects not governed solely by phase contrast may also influence creep response.
